title: 301 vs 302 Redirects: Which One to Use | KivoReach
description: The difference between permanent and temporary redirects, how Google treats each one, and how to avoid long redirect chains when you move pages.

article.summary: Moving a page? The type of redirect tells search engines whether the move is permanent. Here is how to choose, and how to keep redirects short.
article.author: KivoReach
takeaways: Use a permanent redirect (301 or 308) when a page has moved for good.
Use a temporary redirect (302, 303 or 307) only when the original address will come back.
Keep chains short: Google's crawlers follow up to 10 redirect hops by default.

blocks.text: 301 vs 302 redirects: which one to use

blocks.html: A redirect sends visitors and search engines from one address to another. It is how you keep old links working when a page moves, a site changes domain or you switch from http to https.
Server-side redirects come with a status code. The code tells search engines whether the move is permanent or temporary, and that changes which address Google shows in its results.

blocks.caption: Redirect status codes and what they signal
rows: The new address should be shown in results
A page or site has moved for good
A permanent move where the request method must not change
A page is briefly elsewhere and will come back
Sending a visitor to another page after a form
A temporary move where the method must not change

blocks.html: A common mistake is using a temporary 302 for a permanent move. The original address can then stay in search results instead of the new one.

A chain is when one redirect leads to another, and another. Google's crawlers follow up to 10 redirect hops by default, but each extra hop slows visitors down and adds a chance of failure. Point every old address straight to its final destination.

blocks.caption: A two-hop chain: better to send the first address straight to the last one.

blocks.text: Moving a page: step by step

items.title: List the old and new addresses
items.html: One line per page that moves.

items.title: Add permanent redirects
items.html: From each old address directly to its new address.

items.title: Update your own links
items.html: Change internal links and your sitemap to the new addresses, so visitors do not need the redirect.

items.title: Test every old address
items.html: Check that each one reaches the right page in one hop with a 200 status at the end.

blocks.html: Our free Redirect and Status Checker follows any address hop by hop and shows every status code until the final page.

blocks.question: How long should I keep a redirect?
blocks.answer: Keep permanent redirects in place for as long as people and other sites might still use the old address. Removing them too early breaks old links.
